report.executive_summary: AMD and NVIDIA are both developing AI accelerators, with AMD focusing on memory capacity and bandwidth improvements, while NVIDIA emphasizes co-designed platforms and high-performance computing.

competitors.name: NVIDIA
competitors.summary: NVIDIA offers a range of AI accelerators including the Vera Rubin NVL72 and Groq 3 LPX, with co-designed platforms for high-performance computing.

competitors.name: AMD
competitors.summary: AMD is introducing the Instinct MI325X accelerators with enhanced memory capacity and bandwidth, aiming to compete with NVIDIA's offerings.

recent_developments.text: AMD's Instinct MI325X accelerators offer 256GB of HBM3E memory and 6.0TB/s bandwidth, surpassing NVIDIA's H2001 in memory capacity and bandwidth.
NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 integrates multiple GPUs, CPUs, and networking components to scale AI performance across data centers.

market_signals.text: AMD's MI325X accelerators are positioned to challenge NVIDIA's dominance in AI performance with significant improvements in memory and bandwidth.
NVIDIA's co-designed platforms, such as Vera Rubin, highlight its focus on integrated AI and high-performance computing solutions.

risks.text: AMD's upcoming MI450 and MI455X accelerators may face challenges in competing with NVIDIA's established ecosystem and performance benchmarks.
NVIDIA's reliance on HBM memory may limit scalability compared to AMD's potential advancements in memory technology.

sources.title: AMD introduces new AI accelerators and networking solutions
sources.snippet:
AMD+0.22%

SAN FRANCISCO - Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: NASDAQ:AMD) unveiled a suite of new products on Thursday aimed at enhancing AI infrastructure performance, including the AMD Instinct MI325X accelerators and networking components like the AMD Pensando Salina DPU and Pollara 400 NIC (NASDAQ:EGOV). These offerings are designed to meet the growing demands of AI applications and data centers. [...] The AMD Instinct MI325X accelerators, built on the AMD CDNA 3 architecture, promise to deliver significant improvements in AI performance, featuring 256GB of HBM3E memory and 6.0TB/s bandwidth. This represents an increase in memory capacity and bandwidth compared to previous models, with the MI325X offering 1.3 times the peak theoretical FP16 and FP8 compute performance. [...] AMD's growing presence in the cloud computing sector is further emphasized by its recent collaboration with Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). AMD's Instinct MI300X accelerators will power OCI's new AI supercluster, designed to handle complex AI workloads. Early adopters of this offering include Fireworks AI, which has effectively scaled its services using the enhanced memory capacity of the AMD Instinct MI300X.

sources.title: AMD's next-generation AI chips set to power 2026 data ...
sources.snippet:
By Ashish Negi

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ: AMD) is preparing to launch the next generation of its AI accelerators in the second half of 2026, introducing the Instinct MI450 alongside the Helios rack-scale platform (MI455X), both part of the MI400 series. The rollout marks the chipmaker’s latest push to challenge the dominance of Nvidia in the rapidly expanding market for AI computing hardware. [...] Beyond accelerators, AMD is also preparing to introduce its next-generation “Venice” server CPU in the second half of 2026, extending the company’s push into the data-center processor market. Analysts expect the new chip to support continued share gains in servers, lifting data-center server revenue by about 40% year-on-year to $12.8 billion.

Taken together, Visible Alpha consensus forecasts point to total data-center revenue rising 73% to $28.7 billion in 2026. [...] Analysts estimate AMD could ship roughly 258,000 MI400 series units in 2026, with an average selling price of about $30,926. High-volume deployments, particularly for inference-heavy AI workloads, are expected to drive a step-change in profitability. Visible Alpha consensus points to data-center operating income rising to about $9.4 billion in 2026, up from $3.6 billion last year, with segment operating margins projected at 31.04%.

sources.title: Top 12 NVIDIA GPUs for AI Training & Inference in 2026
sources.snippet:
NVIDIA also provides workstation and consumer-grade GPUs, such as the RTX 6000 Ada Generation, RTX A6000, and GeForce RTX series. These are not purpose-built data center AI accelerators and rely on GDDR memory rather than HBM, but they can effectively support model experimentation, fine-tuning, and mid-scale inference at a lower cost.

When choosing AI infrastructure, organizations should focus on memory type and how well the system can scale: [...] Choose from the NVIDIA L40S GPU and NVIDIA H100 NVL to power generative AI workloads, train large language models (LLMs), and run high-throughput inference with strong memory bandwidth and multi-GPU scaling. While next-generation Blackwell GPUs with HBM3e lead frontier AI research, Atlantic.Net focuses on production-ready Hopper-based H100 NVL systems and balanced L40S accelerators that deliver reliable enterprise AI performance today. [...] NVIDIA AI GPUs empower developers to build and optimize a wide range of AI applications. These GPUs enable efficient training and deployment of machine learning models for tasks such as computer vision, natural language processing, and robotics.

Developers can utilize NVIDIA’s software stack, including CUDA, TensorRT, and the TAO Toolkit, to streamline workflows and improve performance. These tools facilitate model optimization, precision tuning, and integration into production environments.

sources.title: AMD Delivers Leadership AI Performance with AMD Instinct MI325X Accelerators
sources.snippet: Built on the AMD CDNA™ 3 architecture, AMD Instinct MI325X accelerators are designed for exceptional performance and efficiency for demanding AI tasks spanning foundation model training, fine-tuning and inferencing. Together, these products enable AMD customers and partners to create highly performant and optimized AI solutions at the system, rack and data center level. [...] SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 10, 2024 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Today, AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) announced the latest accelerator and networking solutions that will power the next generation of AI infrastructure at scale: AMD Instinct™ MI325X accelerators, the AMD Pensando™ Pollara 400 NIC and the AMD Pensando Salina DPU. AMD Instinct MI325X accelerators set a new standard in performance for Gen AI models and data centers. [...] This press release contains forward-looking statements concerning Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) such as the features, functionality, performance, availability, timing and expected benefits of AMD products including the AMD Instinct™ MI325X accelerators; AMD Pensando™ Salina DPU; AMD Pensando Pollara 400; continued growth of AMD's open software ecosystem; AMD Instinct MI350 series accelerators, which are made pursuant to the Safe Harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform
